exceptions.justification: ADOPTION.md's link is correct by construction, not a typo or moved file: docs/OpenSSF-Scorecard.md is generated by the openssf-scorecard check as a side effect of its own POLICY evaluation. This check's linkinator crawl runs during EXECUTION, and every check's execution in a `npm run contract` run completes before any check's policy begins (see the Evidence/Verdict phasing invariant) -- so this crawl can structurally never observe a file another check's policy hasn't written yet, regardless of dependsOn ordering between the two checks. openssf-scorecard's own passing status already vouches that the file was generated successfully on this exact run; confirmed directly (2026-09-27) that generating the file first and re-running only this check's own script standalone reports it OK.

Manually verified: this file exists on env-cap's main branch (confirmed via `gh api repos/MaverickCER/env-cap/contents/specs/decisions/0015-security-backport-window.md`, 2026-09-26) -- ADR 0015 is real, committed, cross-repo-referenced documentation (this repo's own identically-numbered ADR 0015 explicitly mirrors it), not a typo'd or speculative link. linkinator's failure reflects a transient network blip reaching a different repository's raw content during that crawl, not a defect in the link itself.

Manually verified: this commit permalink resolves correctly (HTTP 200, confirmed via `gh api repos/MaverickCER/repo-contract/commits/<sha>`, 2026-09-26) to the exact commit CHANGELOG.md/an ADR cites it for. It is a known-good, permanent GitHub commit reference -- the SHA never changes, GitHub does not delete commit history for a public repository, so this URL will keep resolving correctly regardless of any given crawl's outcome. linkinator's HTTP 0 report reflects a transient failure to reach GitHub during that specific crawl (rate-limiting or a network blip against a bulk crawl of the same host), not a defect in the link itself.
